ai.title: Simplify theme detection priority logic in CLI
ai.summary: Refactored `detectSystemTheme` in `cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts` to use a dedicated `detectPreferredTheme` helper. This replaces the previous nullish coalescing chain with explicit early-return checks for Terminal overrides, IDE, OSC, and Platform themes. The priority order remains Terminal > IDE > OSC > Platform > Default. This change is internal to the CLI utility layer.

eli5.text: When you open the command-line tool, it figures out which color theme to use by checking several possible sources in a fixed order: first any theme you forced in your terminal, then your code editor's theme, then a special theme signal from some terminals, then your operating system's light/dark setting, and finally falling back to dark mode. The way it walks through that decision list was rewritten so the priority checks are clearer and easier to read, but it now picks the same answer it did before. Nothing about the theme you see changes; this just makes the code behind it simpler and less likely to trip up future updates.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use tools, the spacing after the last tool output no longer adds an extra blank line at the end of the group. The CLI now checks whether any non-filler content follows the tool group before deciding to add that gap, so the screen no longer ends with unnecessary vertical whitespace. ai.title: Fix VSCode and Zed theme auto-detection
ai.summary: VSCode theme detection now handles window.autoDetectColorScheme by parsing preferredDarkColorTheme and preferredLightColorTheme, falling back to platform detection if inference fails. Zed theme detection moves system mode fallback to detectZedTheme after extractZedTheme returns null, ensuring platform theme is used when specific mode themes are absent. Removed unused CHAT_THEME_ENV_KEYS and loadThemeOverrides, simplifying chatThemes to use DEFAULT_CHAT_THEMES directly. Updated IDE_THEME_INFERENCE to include 'vs dark' and 'vs light' keywords.

eli5.text: When you open this assistant inside VS Code or Zed, it now does a better job figuring out whether you prefer a dark or light color scheme. Previously, if VS Code was set to automatically switch between dark and light themes based on your system, the assistant might have picked the wrong one or missed your preferred dark/light theme names entirely. Now it checks your configured 'preferred dark theme' and 'preferred light theme' settings directly, and if those aren't set, it falls back to sensing your computer's current dark or light mode. For Zed users, the same improvement applies: when your theme is set to 'system,' the assistant now properly matches your computer's current appearance instead of guessing. The change is live today for anyone using the assistant within VS Code or Zed.

ai.title: Enable nav up/down within input
ai.summary: CLI chat input now supports cursor movement up/down lines via arrow keys. `historyNavEnabled` splits into `historyNavUpEnabled` and `historyNavDownEnabled`, gating navigation only when cursor is at input start/end. `multiline-input.tsx` handles bare up/down keys to adjust `cursorPosition` by effective columns, while `use-keyboard-handlers.ts` delegates history vs line movement based on new state flags. Text wrapping in `multiline-input.tsx` changes from 'word' to 'char' to support precise column calculation.

eli5.text: When typing a multi-line message in the CLI chat, you can now press the up and down arrow keys to move the cursor between lines you've already typed, instead of only using them to recall previous messages from history. The up arrow only jumps to the previous message when your cursor is at the very start of the current line, and the down arrow only recalls the next message when your cursor is at the end of the line, so the two behaviors no longer get in each other's way. You'll notice this right away the next time you write a longer message and reach for the arrows to navigate within it.

This happened because the program simplified how cursor position and text content are updated together behind the scenes, so the rules that keep the cursor on the text rather than floating beyond it work consistently. You can notice this right away if you were previously seeing the cursor land in the wrong place after navigating; the fix applies to everyone typing messages in the CLI interface.
